title: Rhoform Check Report v0
description: The static stage's coverage report for one compilation (spec/language/05-static-types.md, section 1): per pass, what it decided and what it could not, entity by entity. Written by `rhoform check --emit-report DIR` as <stem>.check.json, in rhoform-canonical-json/1, and validated against this schema before it is written. It is never part of design_hash and never changes the IR. Version 0 is UNFROZEN while M2 lands its passes: a landing that fills a section, the waivers or the safety list states their shape here in the same change.

design_hash.description: The design_hash of the IR the checked design serializes to, so a report names the design it covers.

generator.description: The toolchain that wrote the report, as the IR header names it.

sections.description: One section for the model build and one per pass that ran, keyed by the pass's NAME. A pass the run did not reach has no section.

waivers.description: The waivers the design declares and what each matched (T6). Empty until AMB-56 (L5a) lands waivers and states the entry shape.

safety.description: The safety-relevant bonds GA-11 surfaces, waived or not. Empty until the ground-architecture checker (L2c, L5a) states the entry shape.

implemented.description: False for a pass that is not implemented yet; its rows then include the actionable not-implemented row.

rows.description: Sorted by entity, status, reason, actionable, then detail; each row once.

entity.description: The IR entity the row is about: an instance path, a net name or an assertion path, each a node of the source map.

status.description: What the pass concluded about the entity.

reason.description: Why, as a stable kebab-case class; RHO3901 counts actionable rows by it.

actionable.description: True when the author or the toolchain can close the gap; any actionable row raises the compilation's one RHO3901 note. False for an inherent limit, which lives in this report only.

detail.description: Structured facts behind the row: scalars or arrays of scalars, as diagnostic params are.
